title: DPP and related product-traceability regulatory phases
methodology: Curated phase of a specifically evidenced public measure, not a country ranking, generic legal readiness score or automatic maximum of record statuses. Global technical standards and private ecosystem participation are excluded. EU instrument coverage may be joined to member countries for display only. Territorial proxies are explicitly striped and qualified. Grey means not assessed or excluded by filters, not absence of regulation.

phases.applying: Specific sector product-information or traceability duties apply.
phases.adopted: Legal framework adopted; relevant passport rollout is future, conditional or requires further measures.
phases.proposal: Published draft or consultation; final adoption or requirements not established.
phases.early: Official exploration, exporter guidance, public programme or pilot; no DPP duty established by this evidence.

profiles.headline: EU framework adopted; product-specific passport duties phase in
profiles.summary: The ESPR establishes a Digital Product Passport framework, with product coverage and compliance dates set through delegated acts. Battery passports become mandatory from 18 February 2027 for EV batteries, light means of transport batteries and industrial batteries above 2 kWh placed on the market or put into service.
caveats: There is no general ESPR obligation for every product to have a DPP. A working-plan listing is not itself a passport requirement.
Battery passport requirements were not yet operative on the review date. Other sectors have their own instruments, scope and commencement conditions.
EU-country highlighting represents territorial coverage of EU instruments, not a separately completed review of each national implementation.

Related development: the European Product Act product-rules reform remains planned in the Commission tracker. Its intended horizontal DPP approach is under assessment and creates no new current duty; the separately published standardisation proposal has a different procedural status.

profiles.headline: China: NEV battery coding and traceability duties are in force
profiles.summary: Order 73 applies from 1 April 2026 to new-energy-vehicle power-battery recycling and comprehensive utilisation. It requires battery coding and lifecycle information reporting through the national traceability platform. These are sector-specific product-data duties, not a general DPP mandate.
caveats: Article 12 establishes a battery digital-identity system but leaves its detailed measures to separate rules; this review does not establish a completed digital-identity rollout.
The regime concerns NEV power batteries and specified supply-chain actors. It must not be read as equivalent in scope to the EU ESPR.
The general DPP requirements project 20251568-T-469 remains a standards project; it does not extend this battery law to all products.

profiles.headline: United Kingdom · inspect Great Britain and Northern Ireland separately
profiles.summary: Great Britain’s Digital Product Records approach remains under consideration following the 2026 call for evidence and sector consultations.
caveats: The UK outline is a neutral locator. Great Britain-only records do not colour the whole United Kingdom.
This country-level phase describes Great Britain’s proposal track, not a UK-wide enacted DPP duty.
Northern Ireland follows relevant EU instruments under the Windsor Framework; their scope and future passport dates must be assessed separately.

profiles.headline: Northern Ireland: EU framework scope, with product-specific passport dates
profiles.summary: The UK government identifies ESPR and the EU Batteries Regulation as applying in Northern Ireland under the Windsor Framework.
caveats: This does not establish an operative passport duty for every product or extend Northern Ireland’s framework to Great Britain.
Battery passports begin in February 2027; other passport duties depend on the relevant product rules. This is a government scope statement, not a complete incorporation analysis.

profiles.headline: Taiwan: product-information framework adopted; DPP pilots remain voluntary
profiles.summary: Article 22 of the Resource Circulation Promotion Act enables authorities to designate products for information disclosure and unique-code traceability. The amended framework took effect on 17 June 2026, while product designations, deadlines and disclosure methods require further measures. The environmental authority also reports voluntary DPP pilots.
caveats: An enabling provision is not evidence that all products currently need a DPP. This review did not establish a generally operative passport requirement or a specific Article 22 product designation.
Undesignated products may participate voluntarily. Pilot participation is not regulatory coverage.
The official English translation notes that the Chinese text prevails in case of discrepancy; Article 52 defers separate provisions, not Article 22.

sources.title: Taiwan Ministry of Justice — Resource Circulation Promotion Act
sources.locator: Amended 17 June 2026. Article 22: designated product information, unique-code updating, voluntary participation and separate implementing measures. Article 52: commencement and limited deferred provisions.

profiles.headline: Battery-passport implementation consulted
profiles.summary: Norway consulted on changes to its proposed battery regulation, including the passport registry and unique identifier. The reviewed consultation establishes a domestic implementation proposal; the agency's current guidance still makes Norwegian application conditional on incorporation into national rules.
caveats: The April–May 2026 consultation is closed. Final domestic adoption was not established in this review.
EU application dates do not by themselves establish that the same duties apply in Norway.

profiles.headline: Proposed legal basis for digital product passports
profiles.summary: The Federal Council's proposed revision of the Technical Barriers to Trade Act would create a legal basis for introducing digital product passports. The June 2026 announcement opened a consultation that ended in September.
caveats: This is evidence of a legislative proposal, not an existing general Swiss passport obligation.
The consultation deadline has passed; this review did not establish a subsequently enacted text or product-specific duties.

sources.title: Swiss Confederation — modernising the Technical Barriers to Trade Act
sources.locator: Federal Council announcement of 5 June 2026; proposed DPP legal basis; consultation through 28 September 2026.

profiles.headline: Draft Battery Pack Aadhaar guidelines
profiles.summary: The Ministry of Road Transport and Highways published draft guidelines for a battery identity and information system, with electric-vehicle batteries as the defined scope. The document specifies static and lifecycle information associated with a unique battery identifier.
caveats: The reviewed document is expressly marked Draft; a final compulsory instrument was not established.
This is a sector-specific battery proposal, not a passport mandate for all Indian products.

sources.title: Ministry of Road Transport and Highways — Draft Guidelines for Battery Pack Aadhaar
sources.locator: Cover marked Draft; section 2 scope; battery identifier and data-attribute provisions.

profiles.headline: Applying EV battery identification duties — adjacent regime
profiles.summary: The Korean government reports that battery certification and history-management duties took effect on 17 February 2025. Manufacturers assign battery identifiers, and vehicle registration and battery-replacement procedures record them, establishing sectoral traceability relevant to passport development.
caveats: These are adjacent EV battery identification and history duties, not a verified general Digital Product Passport regime.
The classification relies on the ministry's implementation announcement. The consolidated operative legal text was not independently reviewed.
The announcement describes a fuller battery-history information system as planned for 2027; that later system is not treated as already operating.

sources.title: Republic of Korea policy portal / Ministry of Land, Infrastructure and Transport — battery certification and history management
sources.locator: 17 February 2025 announcement; implementation date, manufacturer battery ID, vehicle register and replacement reporting; planned 2027 history system.

profiles.headline: Passport framework adopted; product rollout conditional
profiles.summary: Vietnam's Decree 37/2026 establishes a framework for digital product passports, including identifiers, origin and traceability information, quality and conformity data, and updates through the national traceability infrastructure. The decree entered into force on 23 January 2026; product-specific implementation requires a further roadmap.
caveats: An enabling framework in force is not equivalent to a currently applying passport duty for every product.
The official explanation assigns a product-specific implementation roadmap to further government action. This review did not establish all designated product groups or their deadlines.
The domestic framework does not by itself establish recognition or technical equivalence with EU passports.

sources.title: Vietnam Ministry of Science and Technology — Decree 37: digital technology in quality management and traceability
sources.locator: Sections on digital product passports, minimum information, national traceability portal and product-specific implementation roadmap; effective date 23 January 2026.

profiles.headline: Public battery traceability and interoperability programme
profiles.summary: Japan's NEDO reports a battery traceability platform developed within the Ouranos programme and a demonstration exchanging carbon-footprint information with Catena-X. This is evidence of publicly supported infrastructure and practical interoperability work relevant to DPPs.
caveats: The reviewed programme and demonstration do not establish a general Japanese statutory passport obligation.
A demonstrated carbon-footprint exchange does not establish universal passport interoperability or mutual legal recognition.

sources.title: NEDO — Japan–Europe battery carbon-footprint data exchange demonstration
sources.locator: 31 March 2025 release; Ouranos battery traceability platform, service development and Catena-X carbon-footprint demonstration.

profiles.headline: Official circular-economy inquiry considers digital product information
profiles.summary: Australia's Productivity Commission published its final circular-economy inquiry report in January 2026. It considers digital labels and product passports in its assessment of improved textiles information, alongside recommendations on product stewardship and transparency.
caveats: An inquiry report and its recommendations are not enacted passport requirements.
The report calls for learning from international labelling schemes before determining a domestic approach; no general Australian DPP mandate is established by this record.

profiles.headline: California battery legislation — adjacent, state-level measure
profiles.summary: California's governor announced signing SB 615 within a September 2026 package of electric-vehicle legislation that includes battery-information measures. This is evidence of an adopted state-level measure relevant to battery information and lifecycle management, rather than a national US DPP law.
caveats: Territorial coverage is California only. Colouring the US country outline is a map proxy for this subnational record, not a nationwide obligation.
The signing announcement establishes enactment; the final statutory provisions, operative deadlines and any passport-equivalent requirements were not independently verified in this review.
This is labelled adjacent battery legislation. Federal NIST battery-passport research is a separate research activity and is not evidence of a US regulatory mandate.

profiles.headline: National DPP study and a separate Paraná vehicle pilot
profiles.summary: Brazil's ENIQ 2025–2026 action plan includes a digital product passport benchmarking study. Separately, Paraná's transport authority announced a voluntary digital vehicle-passport pilot in February 2026. These records show public investigation and experimentation rather than an enacted national passport duty.
caveats: Adoption of a policy action plan does not mean adoption of mandatory product passports.
The vehicle pilot is subnational and voluntary; its 120-day planned trial and vehicle-history focus do not establish a national environmental DPP scheme or a completed outcome.
The national plan was rechecked through the official indexed gazette text; direct retrieval of the gazette PDF was unavailable.

profiles.headline: Public innovation procurement for supply-chain credentials
profiles.summary: An Innovative Solutions Canada challenge sought a verifiable-credentials solution for supply chains, including digital product passports. The published competition opened in August 2023 and closed in September 2023, showing official experimentation with the technology.
caveats: The challenge is closed; this review did not establish an awarded, delivered or deployed outcome.
Innovation procurement is not a Canadian legal requirement to issue product passports.

profiles.summary: Türkiye's Ministry of Trade explains the EU Digital Product Passport framework, standardisation work and implementation developments for businesses. This provides an official readiness and trade-policy information signal.
caveats: The guidance describes EU requirements; it does not itself enact a domestic Turkish passport regime.
No transposition or nationwide Turkish DPP obligation is inferred from exporter guidance.

profiles.summary: New Zealand's Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade published a market report explaining the EU circular-economy framework, ecodesign and digital product passports. It helps exporters prepare for developments in their destination market.
caveats: This is official market guidance about the EU, not a New Zealand domestic passport regulation.
The early-policy classification records public readiness activity and does not imply an announced national DPP law.

profiles.summary: Paraná’s transport authority announced a voluntary digital vehicle-passport pilot in February 2026. The vehicle-history trial is a subnational public initiative, not an enacted national product-passport duty.

caveats: This is enterprise and exporter guidance, not a Singapore law requiring product passports or evidence of a national DPP platform.

profiles.headline: Busan: publicly funded battery-passport demonstration
profiles.summary: Busan announced selection for the Ministry of Science and ICT's 2025 public-sector blockchain programme. The city planned a battery-passport platform with demonstrations for charging and safety, performance checks and history management, supported by a 2025 budget of KRW 3.46 billion.
caveats: This is a regional public programme, not a new national DPP obligation. Platform completion or current deployment was not independently established.

Korea's separately reviewed national battery-identification and history duties also form part of the relevant legal context; the local pilot's early phase does not replace their national classification.

profiles.headline: Public product-traceability programme and textile pilot procurement
profiles.summary: Egypt's GOEIC announced a Korean-supported digital inspection and traceability programme, scheduled for 2025–2029, that includes creating DPPs for locally manufactured industrial products. Separately, UNIDO requested textile-SME DPP pilot services in March 2026.
caveats: These are programme and procurement announcements. No generally compulsory Egyptian passport duty or completed national platform was established.
The UNIDO tender closed on 1 April 2026; an award or delivered pilot was not verified. It is not assumed to be part of the GOEIC programme.
The GOEIC announcement was rechecked through the official indexed text; direct page retrieval timed out.

profiles.headline: Government export portal explains EU passport readiness
profiles.summary: Bangladesh's Ministry of Commerce export portal explains EU ESPR and battery-passport developments and the traceability challenges faced by exporters. This establishes an official information and readiness activity; the separate BGMEA and university pilots remain industry and research initiatives.
caveats: This is guidance about access to the EU market, not an enacted Bangladeshi DPP law, adopted national traceability strategy or mandatory national platform.

The portal article draws on export statistics and industry reporting. Its presence on the official portal establishes publication of guidance, not government adoption of the proposals reported from industry.
Government participation in a research roundtable is not treated as proof that a national strategy has been adopted.
